title: Lexeme-level timing probes and KV-cache amortized cost mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add lexeme-level (wordpiece) wall-clock probes and an amortized KV-cache cost mapping pipeline so product teams can attribute latency and token unit cost to individual tokens and cache interactions. Current metrics aggregate at request-level and miss critical spikes caused by cache misses or long kernel invocations; this work will enable per-lexeme histograms, cache-delta annotations, and a low-overhead ingestion path into the metrics/log pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: SDK/runtime emits a compact per-lexeme timing envelope for sampled requests (JSON or protobuf) with fields: lexeme_index, emit_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit (true|false), kv_cache_delta_ms
Server-side collector ingests envelopes without adding >0.5% p99 request latency under production sampling settings
Prometheus-compatible histograms and counters created: lexeme_emit_duration_ms_bucket, lexeme_cache_miss_count, lexeme_cache_delta_ms_summary
Dashboards with token-attribution panels (latency waterfall, cache-impact heatmap) available in Console and linked from model pages
End-to-end docs and example queries for cost reconciliation and alerting added to Confluence
implementation_notes: Phase 1: design lightweight envelope and sampling strategy (1% default sample, configurable per-customer)
Phase 2: add SDK hooks (node/python/go) to emit envelopes over existing tracing transport (OTLP) and as fallback via async HTTP to /v1/internal/lexeme-probes
Phase 3: collector pipeline: enrich with route/model metadata, compute amortized KV-cache cost per lexeme, forward to metrics and logs backends
Phase 4: dashboard panels and alerts with example thresholds for cost regressions and cache-degradation
Instrumentation must avoid heavy allocations in hot path — use preallocated buffers and pooling in runtime hot paths
risks_and_tradeoffs: High-cardinality risk if full token strings are attached — design avoids raw token text and uses lexeme_index + hashed token id
Storage cost: sampling reduces volume; full-sample would be prohibitively expensive
Potential privacy concern for PII in tokens — we will only emit indices and hashed IDs, not raw text
Trade-off between probe accuracy and runtime overhead; default sampling tuned to minimize overhead while catching regressions
